items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Capex + Time = Profits
items.summary: Hyperscaler cloud revenue accelerated to +48% in the second quarter from +39% in the first amid a continued acceleration in enterprise adoption. But consensus continues to underestimate future revenue growth and profitability tied to AI. The math is simple: capex + time = profits.

items.title: Food for Thought: How Are EVs Impacting Brazil's Fuels Demand?
items.summary: The rapid acceleration of EV sales in Brazil raises an increasingly pressing question for the fuels sector: When does this shift begin to structurally and visibly erode Otto Cycle fuels demand? Our answer is that the impact, while modest in aggregate terms, is already real and rising.

items.title: AI Chipmakers to Pivot from Scale-Up to Scale-Out
items.summary: Amid persistent memory shortages, we expect AI chipmakers to increasingly scale out by deploying more GPUs with lower HBM content. We also expect HBM supply to remain tight, as memory suppliers stay disciplined in expanding output amid attractive server economics.

items.title: Metal Matters: Exploring Our Base Case for Gold
items.summary: In our base case, gold prices stagnate or even decline over the next month before rallying to $4,500 an ounce in the fourth quarter and to $5,000 by next year's first half. In this note we look at the reasons for gold's sell-off and what we see shaping prices in the months ahead.

items.title: We're Initiating Coverage of Brunello Cucinelli at Buy
items.summary: We're initiating coverage of Brunello Cucinelli with a Buy rating and a €110 target price. As explored herein, we believe BCU's competitive advantages can endure longer than the market discounts and think current brand-related concerns are overdone, offering an attractive entry point.

items.title: Agnico Eagle Mines' Track Record Keeps Us Constructive
items.summary: We've heard investor worries that Agnico might be starting to overextend, with multiple potential projects on deck and Finland now added to the mix. It's a fair question, but AEM has a long track record running arguably the best gold miner in the world, and so we stick with our Buy rating.

items.title: Equity Markets Positioning Model: Rebuild Continues for Europe
items.summary: Positioning continues to move further out of sync with index performance. Europe stands out as the only major region experiencing a meaningful improvement in risk appetite, supported by fresh long accumulation and favorable earnings delivery. We also offer analysis for the U.S. and Asia.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: What's Next for JPY?
items.summary: The intervention-driven JPY rally may be reaching its limit for now. Ultimately, we see interventions alone as insufficient to turn the JPY tide. That will require a more aggressive policy from the Bank of Japan and/or relief on the fiscal front. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Africa Weekly: The Outlook for the Eco and the Ghana Cedi
items.summary: We consider the implications of the recent announcement by the regional union ECOWAS to move ahead with the introduction of its proposed Eco currency. We also explore evolving changes in the system for auctioning foreign exchange in Ghana and how they might affect the value of the cedi.

items.title: European Equity Strategy: Upgrades, Delivery and Dispersion
items.summary: European earnings have largely met expectations, but an unusually powerful pre-reporting upgrade cycle had already raised the bar for positive surprises, and the market response has been highly discerning: rewards for companies delivering earnings and significant penalties for misses.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Pricing, Financing, Routing and Securing
items.summary: AI lab strategies are shifting from maximizing benchmark scores toward developing models designed to address the full stack of enterprise needs across price, function and speed. This is amplifying enterprises’ need for an orchestration layer for model routing, governance, and security.

items.title: Macro-to-Micro: A Look at Iron Ore's Cost Curve
items.summary: We update our proprietary 2026 iron ore cost curve, which points to an industry effective cost support of ~$85 a ton. Our analysis offers bottom-up support for identifying potential price troughs and periods when equity valuations imply iron ore prices below cost-curve-supported levels.

items.title: We're Downgrading Willis Towers Watson to Neutral
items.summary: We're downgrading Willis Towers Watson to Neutral. The stock now appears to more reasonably discount the outlook, while we lack a differentiated view on the company’s current prospects. We also offer analysis of WTW's investment in AI capabilities.

items.title: U.S. Semis and Semiconductor Equipment: Earnings So Far
items.summary: SOX is up 60% year to date vs. the S&P 500 +9% but down sharply -21% quarter to date vs. S&P500 flat as semis ran into high investor expectations. We look at how demand is holding up for various end markets and recap four key observations and stock actions.

items.title: U.S. Oil & Gas: How Much Power Growth Is Discounted?
items.summary: The sharp pullback in behind-the-meter power providers has erased most year-to-date gains. Is the market correct to assume growth is at risk, or does the sell-off present an opportunity to re-engage on this growth theme? As we explain, we still believe a rising tide can lift all boats.

items.title: Global Quantitative Insights: Inside the Momentum Sell-Off
items.summary: The sharp reversal in Momentum has commanded a lot of attention, with investors rotating away from AI tech-oriented winners and back to valuation-sensitive exposures. We explain why we see this as a reset in leadership rather than a definitive end to the broader Growth and Momentum cycle.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: Dovish Data, Fed Contradict Hawkish Market
items.summary: The Fed opting to hold rates steady and Warsh’s dovish comments led to volatility in markets that had run with a hawkish narrative disconnected from data and the Fed official consensus. The cooling inflation backdrop will be increasingly hard to ignore, keeping 2026 rate hikes unlikely.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: The Messi Theory of Interest Rates
items.summary: Mervyn King gave us the Maradona Theory of Interest Rates to describe active forward guidance; Kevin Warsh is giving us the Messi Theory of Interest Rates for no guidance. As explored herein, Warsh's game plan could allow markets, rather than the Fed, to tighten financial conditions.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Stock Picker’s Dilemma
items.summary: As earnings season rolls along, expected positive surprises remain the norm but with significant single stock volatility on follow-through. One of the more interesting storylines as we wrap up July is the year-to-date performance dispersion between large-cap Growth and Value.

items.title: Amazon Sees AWS "Booming" As Growth Accelerates Meaningfully
items.summary: We emerge from Amazon's second-quarter results incrementally positive. AWS revenue growth accelerated to 37% year over year, spurred by AI revenue, chip sales and accelerating core cloud demand. As discussed in this note, we believe these trends can continue.

items.title: Cross-Border Strength Pushes Mastercard's Margins Higher
items.summary: Mastercard maintained its net revenue growth momentum despite initial headwinds in cross-border travel volumes caused by the Middle East conflict. Looking ahead, we believe that BVNK’s expected third-quarter closing should help MA develop a greater and more integrated stablecoin platform.

items.title: U.S. Application Software: Takeaways From Our CFO Survey
items.summary: Our July CFO survey finds measured optimism as software spend expectations moderated vs. 2025, yet year-to-date budget revisions trended positively. The defining theme? An unmistakable commitment to AI, as the share of organizations allocating 20%+ of budget to AI surged to 33% from 3%.

items.title: U.S. Banks: What to Watch for in the Second Half
items.summary: “What's more important: NIM or NII?” was the debate throughout second-quarter earnings, and we think the conversation is far from settled given the current interest-rate environment. We discuss that as well as what our recent work on 12-month forward-looking fixed-rate repricing suggests.

items.title: U.S. Economics: Another Dovish Inflation Report
items.summary: Core PCE inflation surprised lower at 0.13% month over month following cooler than expected CPI and PPI June reports, as the market narrative that the Fed will need to hike to lower inflation remains divorced from economic data. We see 3.3% year-over-year core PCE as an obvious outlier.

items.title: U.S. Economics: Look at the Trend, Not Level, of Initial Claims
items.summary: While the level of U.S. initial jobless claims is very low and suggestive of still-low layoffs, we think the trend is more important. What we're seeing looks very similar to last year's patterns, and so leaves us expecting a rising unemployment rate in the late summer/early fall.

items.title: UK Economics: A Committee That Really Doesn't Want to Hike
items.summary: The UK left rates unchanged, with July's monetary policy report showing little appetite for raising the bank rate. In their communication, policymakers focused on the growing slack in the real economy to justify their stance. But we think their inflation profile is too weak.

items.title: India Equity Strategy: Reviewing First-Quarter Earnings So Far
items.summary: So far India's first-quarter results have been ahead on earnings though subdued on an absolute basis. Indian equities, particular Tech, have been net beneficiaries in the global AI rotation trade. We review other factors we see at play that leave us staying constructive overall.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: Holding the Line
items.summary: Like Fed Chair Warsh, UK Governor Bailey seems keen to hold. We come out of the July Bank of England meeting with stronger conviction in receiving September MPC SONIA and wary of steepening risk for gilts ahead. We also look at € spreads and the persistent stickiness of Schatz.

items.title: Fed Holds, Warsh Dovishly Points Away From Hikes
items.summary: The Fed held rates steady, as expected, but a surprise came with Warsh's dovish suggestion that he's watching a “broader range” of inflation metrics and that markets may have already done the work of tightening conditions. We continue to expect rate cuts in October, December and January.

items.title: We're Raising Our Microsoft Estimates and Target Price
items.summary: Microsoft’s strong 4Q26 results offered a solid rebuttal to the bear case, with broad-based upside across revenue, earnings, and guidance. Azure and Copilot were standout drivers, while profitability and efficiency improved. We raise our FY27 estimates and lift our target price to $600.

items.title: Japan Equity Strategy: Tech Adjustment in Final Phase
items.summary: Tech stocks corrected sharply from late June, with the Nikkei falling from its highs. Yet high-beta sectors performed well and TOPIX was flat, suggesting broader risk aversion hasn't intensified. Additional downside looks limited, and we still expect a tech-led bull market by year-end.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: The Fed Wants It Steeper
items.summary: Markets may sell some USD in the near term if the Fed stays on hold. Short-term noise doesn’t eradicate our theory of a medium-term U.S.-Iran compromise. We believe the Fed will be comfortable to keep rates unchanged throughout the year. In equities, value continues to outperform growth.

items.title: China Economics: Rate Cut Green Light, Fiscal Acceleration Ahead
items.summary: The Politburo convened its mid-year meeting today to discuss economic issues. The readout came in broadly in line with our expectations — stronger policy rhetoric, but light on specific actions. We summarize our takeaways in this note.

items.title: We're Upgrading Ford to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading Ford to Buy, as we see a turnabout in momentum for the company. Accelerating production of the F-series, lower warranty accruals, an improved aluminum supply and moderating material costs are all positive signs for 2026's second half. We offer further analysis within.

items.title: The Speculative Grade Beat: Reversing Our AI Recommendation
items.summary: Our January overweight call on AI delivered, as AI returned 8.5% against the index's 2.6% through June. But the picture changed in July as AI lagged by nearly 300 basis points, revealing more fragility than headlines initially suggested. We reverse our recommendation to underweight.

items.title: Seagate Delivers a Beat & Raise Quarter
items.summary: Seagate delivered better-than-expected results and guidance, as demand remains exceptionally strong from hyperscalers, AI workloads and growing data retention and a number of factors continue to drive margin expansion. We raise our target price on Buy-rated STX to $1,300.

items.title: Visa Sees Value-Added Services Growth Separating Itself
items.summary: Visa delivered another quarter marked by broad-based outperformance: Consumer spending remained resilient and we particularly note continued acceleration in Value-Added Services. Indications point to FY27 as another strong year above recent growth rates; we raise our target price to $440.
